title: The effect of fine-tuning on language model toxicity
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the propensity of language models to generate toxic content in response to prompts targeting religion, as part of a broader toxicity assessment.
findings: The propensity for models to generate toxic content in response to religion-themed prompts generally decreases after initial instruction-tuning by developers. However, subsequent parameter-efficient fine-tuning on a benign, non-adversarial dataset can inadvertently reverse these safety mitigations, leading to a significant increase in toxicity. The toxicity rates of community-tuned models vary in hard-to-predict ways, even for models fine-tuned for non-English languages.
